title: Speaker gives 20 breakaway Trinamool MPs until 24 November to answer disqualification pleas
dek: The MPs, who announced a merger with the NCPI after the Bengal election, have sought more time at least eight times. Abhishek Banerjee wants them disqualified under the anti-defection law.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla has given 20 MPs elected on Trinamool Congress tickets until 24 November to reply to petitions seeking their disqualification for defecting, and has warned that "appropriate legal steps under the anti-defection rules may follow" if they do not, according to reports. The MPs, who include Sudip Bandyopadhyay, Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar and Satabdi Roy, announced after this year's West Bengal Assembly election, which the Trinamool lost, that they were merging with the Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI).

The petitions were filed under the Tenth Schedule of the Constitution, the anti-defection law, by Trinamool general secretary Abhishek Banerjee. The MPs have asked for more time at least eight times, including on 3 November, and had been granted several extensions, reports said. Their seats in the House have already been rearranged. In September the Supreme Court declined to set a deadline for the Speaker to decide the petitions, according to reports.

Under the Tenth Schedule, members who leave the party on whose ticket they were elected can be disqualified, unless at least two-thirds of the party's members in the House agree to merge with another party. The case is part of the wider split in the Trinamool, whose rival factions have gone to the Election Commission over its name and symbol. The decision rests with the Speaker after the replies are filed.
